title: Arachin daf 5

chapters.title: Tumtum and Androginos in Arachin
chapters.about: Discussion on whether Tumtum and Androginos are subject to valuation laws.

chapters.title: Nidon B'Khvodo and Partial Vows
chapters.about: Evaluating partial vows on limbs and the status of animals like the Parah and Hamor.

chapters.title: Kedushat Guf versus Kedushat Damim
chapters.about: Distinguishing between intrinsic holiness and value-based holiness.

chapters.title: Arachin for a child under 30 days
chapters.about: Whether a vow on a young child is interpreted as a Neder.

chapters.title: Non-Jews and Arachin vows
chapters.about: The debate between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda on non-Jewish involvement.

chapters.title: Historical context of non-Jewish involvement
chapters.about: Explaining the Pasuk regarding non-Jews and the construction of the Bet HaMikdash.

summary: Rabbi Soffer examines the laws of Arachin vows, specifically focusing on the status of a Tumtum and Androginos and whether they are subject to the same valuation laws as others. He further explores the differing opinions of Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda regarding whether a non-Jew can make or be the subject of an Arachin vow, and discusses the implications of these vows for the Bet HaMikdash.
questions: Are a Tumtum and Androginos subject to the laws of Arachin?
Can a non-Jew make an Arachin vow?
Can a non-Jew be the subject of an Arachin vow?
What is the difference between declaring an animal Kodesh for the Mizbeach versus for Bedek HaBayit?
Why does the Gemara discuss the historical involvement of non-Jews in the construction of the Bet HaMikdash?
